#1777. Cisse sheds light on Mancini’s call, impressions of Italy camp and Milan Scudetto desire

Alphadjo Cisse did his first press conference as a member of the senior Italian national team, responding to questions on a number of topics.

Cisse has been called up for the first time by Roberto Mancini, having made a sensational start to the season in his first year in Serie A, which came after recovering from a serious muscle injury that kept him out for the entire second half of last season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The 20-year-old has already scored eight goals across all competitions, with five coming in the league. The most recent of these was against Genoa on Sunday, and now there is talk of a renewal offer from Milan in order to reward his development but also fend off interest from the Premier League.

Cisse spoke at a press conference from the Azzurri headquarters at Coverciano, alongside former Milan man Mattia Liberali, with whom he played in Catanzaro. His comments were relayed by TMW.

What are your feelings after the last few months?

“I always want to demonstrate my qualities. I’ve had some very intense months and I hope to have many more like them.”

What are the strengths and weaknesses of Liberali?

“His play, his shooting. His final pass is one of his best qualities. As for his flaws, I’d say he’s a bit touchy.”

Did you expect to be the top scorer among Italian players?

“Last year’s injury was a difficult time, but I handled it well. I was very confident about coming to Milanello to showcase my skills, and that helped me a lot. Choosing Catanzaro in 2025 was a very easy decision. Polito and Aquilani wanted me, and it was the right choice. I needed playing time.”

“I can play anywhere in attack. As for the specific role, I don’t know if it’s better to say. I like playing in all positions.”

What impression did entering Coverciano give you?

“It’s great to be here, a great responsibility. We’ll have the opportunity to get to know each other in the coming days.”

“My teammates welcomed me very well, but there’s certainly a big difference between Serie B and Serie A. I owe Aquilani a lot, he’s given me a lot and given me a lot of confidence. I’m sorry for him [after he was sacked by Sassuolo], but he’ll definitely have a great coaching career.”

You’re more about talent than physicality, is anything changing?

“Quality is always important. Now in Italy, many young players are emerging, and we’re trying to give them more confidence.”

“For Milan, winning is the priority, the Scudetto like any other competition. Winning is the norm and you can’t neglect any competition. At Milan you have to win everything.”

“Every coach has left me with something. Aquilani had a huge impact last year. Mancini? He welcomed me and encouraged me to train well. Baldini helped me a lot, even though I only worked with him for two weeks. He left me with a lot.”

“Modric would be too obvious… I say Gila.”

Are you aiming to start at San Siro against France?

“The coach will decide. I’m a guy with a lot of ambition, and being here with the national team is a source of pride.”

What kind of game do you expect against France?

“They need no introduction, but Italy always aims to win. Qualifying for Italy should be the norm.”

“Without a doubt, Balotelli, he’s always been a point of reference for me in the national team.”

Do you feel ready to be a point of reference here right away?

“I like pressure, and I think I’ve got the strength to handle it. There are some important players here, some of them have won the European Championship, and you have to show respect. You have to take things one step at a time. The first thing to focus on is making your debut, and then we’ll see.”

#1776. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#1775. Mauricio Pochettino: Career, salary, tactics, clubs and trophies ahead of Man United appointment

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 12 Nov 2026 17:54

Manchester United are closing in on Mauricio Pochettino after sacking Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, having reportedly reached a verbal agreement in principle with the Argentine and prepared to pay to secure his release from the United States Soccer Federation.

Pochettino is currently head coach of the United States men's national team, a role he took up in September 2024 before signing a contract extension that will keep him in the position through the 2030 World Cup.

If confirmed, the move would see United become the seventh senior managerial job of the Argentine’s career, following spells at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the United States.

With that in mind, Sports Mole takes a look at Pochettino's managerial career, salary, tactics, trophies and top scorers, as well as why he left Tottenham and what United could expect.

Pochettino began his managerial career at Espanyol in January 2009, leaving by mutual consent in November 2012 before joining Southampton in January 2013 and moving to Tottenham on a five-year contract in May 2014.

The 54-year-old replaced Thomas Tuchel at PSG in January 2021 but left in July 2022, before taking charge of Chelsea in 2023 and departing by mutual consent in May 2024 following reported tensions over the club's direction and squad-building strategy.

Pochettino succeeded Gregg Berhalter as USMNT head coach after the 2024 Copa America, with the opportunity to lead the team at the 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States, Canada and Mexico, forming a major part of the appeal.

Tottenham sacked Pochettino on 19 November 2019 with Spurs 14th in the Premier League after just three wins from their opening 12 games, barely six months after he had led them to the Champions League final.

Then-chairman Daniel Levy said the board was extremely reluctant but believed the decision was in the club’s best interests, following a League Cup defeat to Colchester United and a 7-2 home thrashing by Bayern Munich.

The problems dated back to the summer of 2018, when Spurs became the first Premier League side not to sign a player during a transfer window, and Pochettino had warned of a painful rebuild after the Madrid final.

The Argentine manager also admitted in Singapore that he would probably have left had Spurs won the Champions League.

Heavily influenced by Marcelo Bielsa, Pochettino favours a high-pressing, attacking style built around a preferred 4-2-3-1 formation, with his teams encouraged to build from the back and create chances through movement in the final third.

At Tottenham, that developed into a flexible system with advanced full-backs providing width, while Spurs recorded the lowest number of passes allowed per defensive action in the Premier League in both 2015-16 and 2016-17.

Pochettino has also shown tactical flexibility, using a 4-1-4-1 to beat Manchester City  in October 2016 and a more cautious mid-block during Tottenham's run to the 2018-19 Champions League final.

With the USMNT, he used a 4-2-3-1 in their 4-1 win over Paraguay at the 2026 World Cup, while also earning a reputation for developing young players such as Dele Alli and Eric Dier and giving academy graduates including Harry Winks and Josh Onomah opportunities in the first team.

Southampton finished eighth in 2013-14, their highest league finish since 2002-03, while Tottenham won no trophies under Pochettino, losing the 2015 League Cup final and 2019 Champions League showpiece but finishing second in 2016-17.

At Paris Saint-Germain, he won all three trophies of his managerial career, lifting the Trophee des Champions and Coupe de France in 2021 before claiming the Ligue 1 title in 2021-22.

Chelsea finished sixth in 2023-24 and lost the League Cup final to Liverpool after extra time, meaning Pochettino’s only season at Stamford Bridge ended without silverware.

With the USMNT, he lost the 2025 Gold Cup final 2-1 to Mexico before topping Group D at the 2026 World Cup, only to suffer a 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the last 16.

Southampton's Rickie Lambert and Jay Rodriguez each finished as the club's leading league scorer with 15 goals in 2012-13 and 2013-14 respectively, although Lambert's tally covered the full 2012-13 campaign, which began under Nigel Adkins, while Harry Kane scored 169 goals under Pochettino at Tottenham, representing 67.6% of the 250-goal club tally.

Kane won the Premier League Golden Boot in 2015-16 and 2016-17 and became the first Tottenham player to score at least 20 goals in five successive seasons during Pochettino's reign.

Kylian Mbappe top-scored for PSG in 2021-22 with 28 league goals, while Cole Palmer netted 22 times in the Premier League for Chelsea in 2023-24 to finish as the club's leading scorer.

Folarin Balogun led the USMNT scoring charts at the 2026 World Cup with three goals, including two against Paraguay, despite having his one-match suspension following a red card against Bosnia and Herzegovina suspended by FIFA.

Pochettino reportedly earns around $6m (£4.5m) a year as USMNT head coach, making him the highest-paid coach in US Soccer history, and received $5.02m (£3.8m) during his first seven months in the role, including a $2.5m (£1.8m) bonus.

The Argentine’s salary at United is unconfirmed, but he could rank among the Premier League's best-paid managers, with a package potentially comparable to those of Xabi Alonso, Oliver Glasner and Enzo Maresca, whose reported annual salaries are between £10m and £11.5m.

United would reportedly need to trigger a release clause of around $10m, or approximately £7.4m, in his US Soccer contract, with further compensation required if the club also wants to bring members of his coaching staff to Old Trafford.

At Tottenham, Pochettino reportedly earned up to £8.5m a year and was linked with a severance payment estimated at around $16m following his dismissal in 2019. At PSG, he reportedly earned approximately €1.1m gross per month before agreeing a termination settlement worth around €10m for himself and his coaching staff combined in 2022.

Pochettino has long been admired by Manchester United, with the club previously considering him as a managerial candidate in 2016 and again in 2018, while Chelsea and Real Madrid were also linked with the Argentine at different points during his Tottenham reign. Spurs' final match at the old White Hart Lane in 2017 was a 2-1 win over United.

When United sacked Jose Mourinho in December 2018, Pochettino was among the leading candidates to replace him permanently, only for the job to initially go to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, who started out as caretaker.

Fast forward to November 2026, and after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday, ESPN reported Pochettino as United's favoured candidate, with Eddie Howe, Kieran McKenna and Julian Nagelsmann also among the names being considered as the hierarchy met Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco.

#1773. Manuel Akanji questions Cesc Fabregas's Como success after Inter win

By Naim Beneddra | 12 Nov 2026 17:57

Former Manchester City defender Manuel Akanji has questioned the excitement surrounding Cesc Fabregas's Como, insisting that the Italian club still have plenty to learn despite their impressive Champions League campaign.

Como have emerged as one of Europe's surprise packages this season, producing some remarkable results under the former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder, including a stunning 9-1 victory over Lens in the Champions League.

However, their progress has not convinced Akanji, who helped Inter Milan secure a 2-0 victory over Fabregas's side at San Siro on Sunday.

The Switzerland international has now won all four matches he has personally played against Como, a record he believes offers a different perspective on the growing reputation of the ambitious Serie A club.

Speaking during Switzerland's international training camp on Wednesday, Akanji delivered a pointed assessment of Fabregas's team, although he also acknowledged the quality they have demonstrated since returning to Italy's top flight.

Asked about the so-called 'Como phenomenon', Akanji made little attempt to hide his scepticism.

"What phenomenon? I've played against them four times and won all four," the defender said during his international press conference, as reported by Tuttomercatoweb.

"To me, they're not that big of a phenomenon."

Akanji was referring to his personal record against Como, rather than suggesting that Inter had won every meeting between the clubs.

Indeed, the Nerazzurri were held to a goalless draw in the first leg of last season's Coppa Italia semi-final, a match in which Akanji did not feature.

The former City defender nevertheless recognised Como's progress under Fabregas, particularly their ability to compete in European football.

"Of course, they've adapted very well to Serie A and they also won 9-1 in the Champions League," he continued.

"They're a very strong team, but in the games I've played against them, they didn't seem superior to other teams.

His remarks followed another disappointing encounter with Inter for Fabregas, whose side arrived in Milan on a six-match winning streak across all competitions.

Como had attracted widespread attention with their extraordinary success against Lens in France, where Tasos Douvikas scored a hat-trick as the Italian club recorded one of the most emphatic victories of this season's Champions League league phase.

They had also defeated Manchester United 4-1 in Europe, further demonstrating their ability to trouble established opponents.

However, Inter proved a significantly more difficult challenge.

Goals from Pio Esposito and Marcus Thuram inside the opening 20 minutes gave Cristian Chivu's side control of Sunday's contest, and Como were unable to produce a response.

The result extended Inter's impressive record against their regional rivals and ended Como's recent winning run.

Despite the sharp tone of Akanji's assessment, Fabregas had already acknowledged the difference between the two teams.

Before Sunday's encounter, the former Spain international described Inter as the strongest side in Italy and suggested that Como's development was still a work in progress.

Following the defeat, he offered another candid assessment of his team's shortcomings.

"We didn't start the game well, we made a few mistakes and we weren't confident," Fabregas told DAZN.

"We have to congratulate Inter, who played much better than us."

The Como manager highlighted the difficulty of competing against opponents with greater experience, particularly as his squad adjust to the demands of playing domestic and European matches every few days.

He also identified Inter's ability to exploit turnovers as a decisive factor in the defeat.

"They're very strong in transition, the strongest in Europe," Fabregas explained, acknowledging that mistakes in possession had left his players exposed.

His response was notably measured, with the 39-year-old refusing to search for excuses despite the disappointment of losing a significant league encounter.

Fabregas has transformed Como into an ambitious outfit capable of competing with some of Europe's established names, with young talents such as Nico Paz playing important roles in their development.

Their performances have raised expectations considerably, particularly after the historic victory over Lens.

However, Inter remain a difficult obstacle for the former Premier League midfielder, who has yet to record a victory against the Milan giants since becoming Como manager.

Akanji also acknowledged that Inter have experienced defensive problems of their own this season.

The Swiss international admitted that individual mistakes had contributed to several goals conceded by Chivu's team, but said internal discussions following their recent derby defeat to AC Milan had helped improve matters.

Inter responded with consecutive victories over Feyenoord and Como, scoring five goals without conceding.

For Fabregas, the challenge is to ensure that Sunday's setback does not interrupt his team's wider progress.

Como will resume their Champions League campaign against AEK Athens on November 24, when they will have another opportunity to demonstrate the qualities that have made them one of Europe's most talked-about emerging teams.

#1771. Journey to Wembley: Halifax set sights on winning more fans and climbing mountain to the Football League as their FA Cup adventure is ended by route-one Cheltenham

By IAN HERBERT AT EV CHARGER POINTS STADIUM

Published: 21:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 18:05 EST, 9 November 2026

The FC Halifax manager John McGrath’s father-in-law is the top British mountaineer Alan Hinkes OBE and he knows that he has something of a summit of his own to scale, as he walks straight from the team bus to the pitch, set in the lee of Cheltenham’s mist-shrouded Cleeve Hill.

McGrath is all-too familiar with this setting. He brought his Buxton team here in the FA Cup's second round last season and was on the fringes of a major upset – 2-1 up at half-time – before watching the game fall away.

Cheltenham are a much stronger club, 12 months on, but our few weeks with McGrath, an Irishman who 25 years ago was playing for Aston Villa against Liverpool in the Premier League, reveal his ambition for the National League side he joined this summer.

We’re alongside him and FC Halifax on our journey to Wembley, told through all 13 rounds, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the team who knock them out, all the way to the final.

A mist-veiled evening at Halifax’s Shay Stadium, a few weeks back, revealed much about 46-year-old McGrath. He arrives with his two-man coaching team for a Q&A with fans who, when the evening’s proceedings are finished, form a long and orderly queue to talk to him, one-on-one. The team’s four-hour drive to Southend awaits the following morning. But McGrath has no eye for the clock.

This managerial journey is one he hadn’t anticipated when, aged 32, a serious foot injury ended his long career with Burton Albion. He secured a master’s degree in broadcasting and media at Staffordshire University and had begun spots for Sky Sports and BBC local radio, yet here he is on ‘the grass’ he'd never wanted to leave.

His wife Fiona is Director of Public Realm at Islington Council and their time together is some weeks limited to a coffee at Doncaster station, near their home, when he drops her before daybreak. ‘It’s our little half an hour,’ he relates. ‘We’re ships that pass in the night.'

Cheltenham edged out FC Halifax 2-0 in front of 2,961 fans to reach round two

Cheltenham boss Steve Cotterill shakes hands with Halifax manager John McGrath

Ground staff put up the goalposts at EV Charger Points Stadium, also known as Whaddon Road

His club’s fans are partisan – 350 are here – and yearn for League Two, though there’s not a fortune at McGrath’s disposal. The club’s owner David Bosomworth was at the club when it went bust in 2008 and they say that experience left him painfully aware of the need for sustainability. Fair enough. Bosomworth has declined to speak to us. He is not at Cheltenham.

An hour out from kick-off, McGrath is handing out training vests for the warm-up as well as observing things – it’s a modest backroom team – and that defeat last season perhaps plays on his mind. ‘Cheltenham tweaked it that day and personally, I think I should have done the same,’ he says. ‘I’m a better manager, 12 months on.’

The club could badly use the £50,000 prize money that a win here would bring, not to mention the accompanying shot of exhilaration.

McGrath already belongs in the margins of the tournament’s history. He and his son, Jay, a Doncaster Rovers player, became the first father and son to play in the same team in an FA Cup game when McGrath, Mickleover Sports' player-manager for their preliminary-round win against Coventry Sphinx in 2019, fielded his 17-year-old boy.

Halifax seem up for this challenge. Their players go looking for their kit in their bus's luggage compartment before the driver has jumped out to produce the key. But Cheltenham have come a long way in the past year.

The former Burnley owner Mike Garlick bought the club 15 months ago and his investment strategy has echoes of the methods which made the Turf Moor club a Premier League side for seven out of eight years. Manager Steve Cotterill, quickly installed by Garlick, was briefly with him at Burnley.

Cheltenham fans arrive at the ground with their side riding high, fifth in League Two

Halifax fans cheer on their side but their Cup run is over - they travel to Kidderminster next Saturday in the National League

Mike Garlick bought Cheltenham last year and quickly installed Cotterill as manager

There’s an air of optimism around the place, as head groundsman Paul Gibson attends to some stray grass cuttings with a leaf blower and husband and wife team Gerry and Hannah Oldham sort the kit.

The ground staff, with their distinctive West Country burr, take enjoyment from several attempts at installing the goalposts before getting them upright. Mascot ‘Whaddney the Robin’ is limbering up for a leisurely lap of the stadium.

Garlick suggests we use Cotterill’s office as a quiet place to talk as the stadium begins to fill up. He tries calling the manager for his consent to do so but Cotterill’s phone rings out in the room.

It turns out Cotterill is receiving calls on his watch. This is a source of some humour as Cotterill eventually barrels into the office, exhibiting his usual energy. The two men clearly get on.

Extra preliminary round, August 8: Nelson 3-2 Stockport Georgians

Preliminary round, August 22: Witton Albion 1-0 Nelson

1st qualifying round, September 5: Avro 0-2 Witton Albion

2nd qualifying round, September 19: South Shields 7-0 Witton Albion

3rd qualifying round, October 3: Buxton 0-2 South Shields

4th qualifying round, October 17: Halifax 3-2 South Shields

1st round, November 7: Cheltenham Town 2-0 Halifax

Garlick looks more at home here than at Burnley. He also owns Spanish third-tier side Antequera CF and a club in Gibraltar but yearned for this kind of environment and Cheltenham, tumbling towards the EFL exit last year, badly needed help.

‘I missed English football,’ Garlick says. ‘I thought this was a club where I could make a difference and have some impact. When I came in, we had four points from nine games and were bottom of the league. It was hard work last season, but the fans seem happy for me to be here.

'Everyone who comes up to me says “thanks for helping the club,” which is nice. I never quite got that at Burnley to be honest. I’ve probably got more thanks here in 12 months than in 17 years on the board at Burnley. But that’s football isn’t it?!’

There’s been substantial investment in the training ground, a new stadium hospitality lounge, and Cotterill’s contacts have contributed to some eye-catching signings including veteran former Villa forward Andreas Weimann from Rapid Vienna.

Halifax start the game well, with wingers Ben Tollitt and Connor Douglas both flying and Conor Carty, the Irish forward who has been a revelation this season, ready to receive. Twice, they go close in the early stages. But Cotterill has a very uncomplicated route-one method in place and whip-fast striker Kirsten Otchere, on loan from Leicester City, looks lethal.

Will Flint’s string of fine interventions for Halifax is matched by the excellence of goalkeeper True Grant but Otchere crosses from the left for Jake Evans to score, left-footed.

This time McGrath does change things, adjusting the defensive line to quell Otchere’s threat after half time. Cotterill, whose colourful touchline antics include shoving his full-back out of the way when he blocks his line of view, grows concerned as Cheltenham’s attacking threat fades and Halifax dominate.

Carty nets from a Douglas’ crosses but is offside. Halifax lack the moment of class to convert superiority into goals. Substitute George Miller’s late header ended Halifax’s tournament for another year.

Halifax's Ben Tollitt battles for possession but his side cannot find a way through Cheltenham

McGrath and his Halifax players applaud the travelling supporters after their Cup exit

The Cheltenham fans flood out into suburban Whaddon Road fortified in their belief that something is building. ‘An FA Cup run is great for morale and also a massive contribution to the finances, because we’re hopefully going to strengthen again in January and the summer,’ says Garlick.

A foggy trip up the M6 awaits Halifax, though McGrath brings both a hinterland and perspective to the quest of start filling the famous old Shay Stadium once more and pushing closer to the fourth tier after 24 years away. His father-in-law was the first Briton to climb all the world's 8,000m mountains, in the Himalayan and Karakoram ranges of Nepal, Tibet and Pakistan.

‘He’s one of the best in the world,’ McGrath relates. ‘And however tough it is being a footballer or football manager, you try sitting on the side of Mount Everest for three months.

‘There’s a rumour building in our town that we play good football, that there’s goals to be seen at our stadium and a bunch of talented young men are representing the club in the right way.

'We want to get another 800 fans a week through the door and kick the club up the division and into the Football League. We think we can do that.’

#1770. Report: Julian Ward in talks with Liverpool duo as huge call needs to be made

Julian Ward has a lot to try and sort out at Liverpool over the next year or so.

The Englishman took over from Richard Hughes as Liverpool's sporting director and inherited a team he probably didn't think he'd have to improve all that much.

But, since they're currently fourth in the Premier League, it's clear that improvements can be made.

Of course, the over £150 million that Liverpool spent on new players this summer has helped improve things at Anfield but, since their rivals also had the same idea, the gap between the Reds and the actual title challengers is still growing.

This is obviously worrying as, with the sheer amount of money that they spent on new players, you'd have hoped that they'd be better than they were last term.

Changes can be made at any point in the season so, the fact that Ward is already trying to plan ahead for the future is definitely good news.

Julian Ward is in contact with Virgil van Dijk and Alisson's agents

In June 2027, many contracts from players within Liverpool's first-team squad are set to expire.

The last couple of years at Anfield have been filled with players leaving for free and, while the Reds can afford to let some talent go for nothing, they can't make it a yearly thing.

Ibrahima Konate and Trent Alexander-Arnold are the two biggest-named players to have exited L4 recently.

However, this June, Alisson and Virgil van Dijk could both be on the chopping block.

The contracts of both players expire in 2027 and, right now, there are now talks taking place between the club and the players about extending their stays.

That is, unless this update from The Athletic journalist James Pearce is accurate.

"It was April 2025 before Salah and Van Dijk penned two-year extensions and, soon after, there was clarity regarding Alexander-Arnold’s desire to leave his boyhood club for Real Madrid," he wrote.

"There is unlikely to be a quick resolution this time, either — despite the fact that Van Dijk and Alisson could sign pre-contract agreements with clubs overseas in just 51 days.

"It makes sense for all parties to wait and see how things unfold in the coming weeks and months. Respect abounds and relationships are strong, with dialogue ongoing between sporting director Julian Ward and the pair’s camps.

"Given their legendary status, there will be a growing clamour externally for the club to do whatever it takes to keep Van Dijk and Alisson on board.

"However, Ward’s job involves taking the emotion out of the decision-making process, with renewal terms based on what he believes they have left to offer at the highest level beyond next summer rather than what they have already achieved at Anfield."

Liverpool must keep Alisson and Virgil van Dijk at Anfield

This season, Alisson and Van Dijk have been as important as ever.

Although there have been a couple of times this term when both players have made mistakes, more often than not, they've been some of Liverpool's best performers.

Of course, each of them are getting to the twilight stages of their careers now but, it would still be extremely hard to replace either of them.

Of the two, Alisson is probably the most replaceable but, with how well he's performed this season, he's making his case to be seen as one of the world's best goalkeepers again.

Van Dijk is obviously one of a kind. The Dutchman has been the rock at the centre of Liverpool's defence for as long as anyone can remember and, even if someone such as Giovanni Leoni ends up making his way into Iraola's plans this season, he'll still be nowhere near the level the Dutchman is.

There are a lot of questions that still need to be answered by all he involved parties but, for now at least, Liverpool should do everything they can to keep the duo at Anfield.

#1769. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1768. Sweden vs Bosnia-Herzegovina - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 18:57, Last updated: 13 Nov 2026 20:08

The top two in Group B4 of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League will lock horns on Saturday evening, as Sweden welcome Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Both teams are bidding to secure first position in the section, which would mean automatic qualification to League A for the next Nations League.

Sweden have a record of three wins and one draw from their four matches in Group B4, which has left them top of the section on 10 points, two points ahead of second-placed Bosnia-Herzegovina with two games left to play.

As it stands, the Blue and Yellows will secure promotion to League A, but second spot in the group would lead to them dropping into the promotion playoffs.

Graham Potter's side opened their Group B4 campaign with back-to-back wins over Romania and Poland at the end of September, before drawing 0-0 with Bosnia-Herzegovina in the reverse match between the two sides at the start of October.

Sweden will enter this match off the back of a win, though, beating Romania 1-0 last time out, and they are now preparing for their final two games against Bosnia-Herzegovina on Saturday and then Poland on November 17.

The Blue and Yellows are bidding to secure promotion to League A for just the second time, having previously competed at that level in 2020-21.

Bosnia-Herzegovina, meanwhile, will also have their eyes on first position and automatic promotion to League A, but they have work to do if that is to be the case.

Sergej Barbarez's side have a record of two wins and two draws from their four matches in the section, with eight points leaving them in second spot at this stage of proceedings.

As it stands, the Dragons are qualifying for the promotion playoffs, but they are only two points off leaders Sweden, so a win in this contest would be huge, while they are four points ahead of third-placed Poland at this stage of proceedings.

Bosnia-Herzegovina drew 0-0 with Poland in their section opener before recording a 4-2 victory over Romania in their second match at the end of September.

The Dragons then drew 1-1 with Sweden at the start of October, before recording a 1-0 victory over Poland in their last match.

Bosnia-Herzegovina form (all competitions):

Sweden are set to have their two star strikers in their starting side on Saturday, with Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres both in line to feature from the first whistle.

Dejan Kulusevski is back in the squad, having returned to fitness with Tottenham Hotspur this season, and the attacker could potentially be handed minutes off the bench.

Alexander Bernhardsson is in line to win his 19th cap, while Yasin Ayari could also potentially feature from the first whistle in this contest.

As for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Tarik Muharemovic is out of the match through suspension, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape for the contest.

Ermedin Demirovic has scored four times in 48 caps for his country, and the 28-year-old is expected to feature in the final third of the field, while there should also be another spot in the side for Haris Tabakovic.

Sead Kolasinac is in line to win his 74th cap for his country, but there is no Edin Dzeko in the squad, with the legendary forward recently announcing his international retirement.

#1767. Report: Liverpool's transfer 'priority' confirms major Andoni Iraola decision

Andoni Iraola has been given a tough hand to deal with during his first season as Liverpool's boss.

The Reds have spent over £600 million across the last couple of years with most fans believing that they'd easily run away with the Premier League title.

That has obviously not been the case. Right now, Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League and find themselves nine points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

And, while this isn't the end of the world, everyone involved with Liverpool would probably prefer them to be a bit more in the title race right now.

So, with the January transfer window just around the corner, changes are expected to occur with several players already being linked with leaving and joining the Reds.

Liverpool are not prioritising the signing of a new centre-back in the future

This summer, a lot of Liverpool's recruitment was focused around shoring up their defence.

But, during the season before that, injuries, coupled with poor form often crippled the Reds in their games and ended with them finishing fifth in the Premier League.

This was obviously miles away from where they needed to be, especially since it was only a season after they'd won the title.

In the end, this poor form led to Arne Slot's sacking and thrusted Iraola into the deep end.

The Spaniard and Richard Hughes made some changes to Liverpool's first-team squad but, some more transfers are needed, especially with how many of their players' contracts are set to expire in June 2027.

So, this latest update from James Pearce is certainly an interesting one.

"Centre-back not a priority for Liverpool." he wrote.

"So highly unlikely they will invest heavily in that area either in Jan or next summer. Jacquet has made a huge impact and big hopes for fellow young CBs Leoni, Ndukwe and Ndiaye."

Virgil van Dijk must be staying if centre-back isn't a priority for Liverpool

Virgil van Dijk is one of the biggest-named players who's contract expires in June 2027.

The Liverpool captain extended his contract by two years back in 2024 but, now that he's only got six months left on his deal, a decision needs to be made.

By the time the 2027-28 season comes around, the Dutchman will be 36 years old so, it's obvious why some questions are being asked about whether he has what it takes to still do it at the top level.

But, thanks to this latest update from Pearce, it seems like Liverpool believe he can.

Because, with Van Dijk and Joe Gomez's contracts running out this summer, there's no way that a new centre-back wouldn't be signed by Liverpool.

Throw in the fact that Ronald Araujo's season-long loan is also going to end in June, the Reds would literally have Giovanni Leoni and Jeremy Jacquet as their starting centre-backs.

And, while both players are incredible, they're not ready to be a centre-back partnership for Liverpool just yet.

Admittedly, Van Dijk has been making the odd mistake recently, but, give him another couple of years to mentor the young defenders coming through, and he could craft them into some of the world's best.

Here's hoping Liverpool come to their senses and come to an agreement with their captain.

#1765. 'I've never revealed the whole story': England fans wouldn't boo me if they knew the truth, says Ben White... as he defends World Cup walkout and rejecting call-ups

Published: 15:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 18:20 EST, 9 November 2026

Ben White believes England fans would not boo him if they knew the truth behind his 2022 World Cup walkout.

The Arsenal defender left the camp in Qatar after the group stages citing 'personal reasons', although a fallout with Gareth Southgate's assistant, Steve Holland, was later reported. He then declined a return to the England set-up while Southgate and Holland were in charge but was included by Thomas Tuchel in March of this year.

However, White was booed by fans inside Wembley when he came on in the second-half of a friendly against Uruguay, only to score his first international goal and then concede a late penalty in a 1-1 draw. He was not selected for the World Cup in North America but is back with the squad ahead of this week's Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

And the 29-year-old, addressing those jeers for the first time, said: 'It was hard to hear, especially because they didn't know the situation, which is kind of what I put my mind to.

'They don't know my situation and it is not really about what I have done, because they don't know why, and if they did they would not be booing or saying these things. I just think about maybe (them) not knowing the full story, and if they did, maybe they wouldn't (boo).'

He added: 'Obviously, a load has been said. I've probably seen all of it. I just think people don't know the full story, because I've never said anything, and I won't put anyone under the bus or share any of that.

Ben White has insisted he would not be booed by England fans if they knew the truth behind his World Cup walkout

White fell out with former England assistant Steve Holland (left) before heading home during the 2022 World Cup

'There were loads of things that happened and communication wasn't great. I don't want to throw anyone under the bus. A lot of people try to do that to me so it's something I wouldn't want to do myself. I think it's probably the best way. It's a bit tricky and not straightforward, but it's amazing to be here now. It's a privilege to be called up.'

White, however, is adamant that he would make the same decision today and leave the World Cup, even if he will not divulge the reasons as to why.

'I don't think I would (do anything different),' he said. 'I think, as a person, I'm quite real, and I made the decision that I would probably continue to make. It's one that I'm not happy about. It wasn't ideal. But it happened, it's time to move on.

'I don't think I am looking to win anyone over or say anything that helps them get back on my side. It is what it is. There are reasons for it and I am just looking forward to playing for England and doing well and looking for success.'

White has spoken publicly about not watching football, and this, too, has been used against him by some supporters.

'It doesn't mean I don't like football, because I do it every day, so I must like it a little bit!' he said. 'It's because I don't watch it, which I think is quite normal for someone that does a job and then doesn't go home and then continue watching that job.

'I don't think anyone knows my personality. I keep that to my loved ones and family. It's all noise when people have an opinion on that stuff. It is not actually me. People don't know me and I like it that way. You give so much to the game, which is intense. I think it's important to keep some bits for yourself. I keep the energy for the people I love.'

England new boy Josh King believes his aptitude for academia gives him an advantage at the start of a burgeoning career.

The Fulham star – who has two Premier League goals this season – linked up with Thomas Tuchel’s squad on Monday morning as one of two fresh call ups alongside Jobe Bellingham.

King was a straight-A student at the renowned independent Hampton School in south London, with alumni including Queen guitarist Sir Brian May and golf pro Paul Casey.

The teenager’s mother, Michelle, is a university lecturer and finishing a PhD on sickle cell disease while his father Steve is a personal injury lawyer.

‘The most important thing about being good academically and education-wise is you’re able to take on information much more quickly,’ King said.

‘You can take on information which might take a bit longer for other people. I think that definitely helps.’

While the 19-year-old was invited to take part in a pre-World Cup training camp in Miami, he is hoping to make his international bow against Croatia on Thursday.

Although a central figure in Fulham’s midfield, a confident King could be utilised wider by Tuchel were he to be given an opportunity across the two-game Nations League camp.

‘There was a buzz around Fulham when I got called up [this week],’ he added. ‘I got off the phone with the boss, ran into the kitchen and started cheering with my dad. I called mum at work and she was screaming in the office. This felt slightly unachievable when I was younger.’

Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane were namechecked as those who helped him settle when introduced to the group in Florida, with King having also studied the likes of Jamal Musiala and Pedri to elevate his own game.

‘The main thing you take is the standards they set,’ he said when reflecting on joining the camp in America. ‘The way they conduct themselves, the way they perform every day, the way they train and the way they take everything seriously.

‘The little things, technical things, the way some people strike the ball, the way some people pass, just little things which you almost take without thinking about it - they also have an impact.

‘On a few occasions I asked “how do you finish this way” or “what do you do in this scenario” and it always helps to add to my game.’

#1764. PSG consider new Marquinhos contract despite defensive succession plans

By Naim Beneddra | 12 Nov 2026 19:18

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly considering offering Marquinhos a new contract, despite having already invested in younger defenders to prepare for the eventual departure of their long-serving captain.

The 32-year-old Brazilian, who joined PSG from Roma in 2013, is currently tied to the French champions until June 2028, when he will be approaching his 34th birthday.

However, according to Le Parisien, the club's hierarchy have raised the possibility of extending his stay beyond that date and have already discussed the matter with his representatives.

The discussions remain at a preliminary stage, with no formal offer reported and the defender's position on a potential extension yet to emerge.

The development is particularly interesting given PSG's efforts to build a younger defensive unit, including the recruitment of Illya Zabarnyi from Bournemouth and the emergence of Willian Pacho and Lucas Beraldo.

Rather than preparing for an imminent change of leadership, the French champions appear willing to consider keeping their most experienced defender for several more years.

Marquinhos remains one of the most influential figures in Luis Enrique's squad, having spent more than 13 years at the Parc des Princes.

The Brazil international has made 531 appearances for PSG, becoming the club's all-time appearance holder and playing a central role in their rise to the summit of European football.

He captained the Parisian side to their historic first Champions League triumph in 2025 and was again part of the team that successfully defended the trophy in 2026.

His longevity has been particularly remarkable considering the extensive changes to PSG's squad over the past decade.

The departures of several established stars have left Marquinhos as one of the few remaining links with the club's earlier era of major investment under Qatar Sports Investments.

His current contract was agreed in May 2023, when PSG announced a new deal running until 2028.

Although that agreement still has more than 18 months remaining, the French champions are reportedly examining whether another extension would be appropriate.

Le Parisien suggests that the initial discussions reflect the confidence PSG continue to place in their captain, both as a defender and as a senior figure within the dressing room.

However, there is no indication that the club have settled on the length or financial terms of a potential agreement.

The report also provides no confirmation that Marquinhos has decided to prolong his career in the French capital beyond his existing contract.

A new deal would nevertheless represent a significant commitment to a player who would be in his mid-thirties by the time any further extension approached its conclusion.

The possibility of retaining Marquinhos for longer comes at a time when PSG have already made substantial investments in the future of their defence.

Zabarnyi joined from Bournemouth in the summer of 2025 for approximately £53.6m, with the Ukraine international viewed as a potential long-term successor to the Brazilian captain.

However, the 24-year-old has struggled to establish himself consistently under Luis Enrique.

His first campaign in Paris failed to meet expectations, and his limited involvement during the opening months of the current season prompted speculation about his future.

The Ukrainian has nevertheless shown signs of improvement while deputising for the injured Marquinhos, leaving PSG with an important decision over his development.

The club also have Pacho, who signed a new contract until 2031 in September, alongside fellow centre-back Beraldo, whose agreement was extended to the same year.

Both players form part of the younger core PSG have assembled under Luis Enrique and sporting adviser Luis Campos.

Paris have continued monitoring emerging defensive talent, with Lens youngster Pierre Ismaelo Ganiou recently linked with the European champions.

However, the interest in younger defenders does not necessarily mean that Marquinhos would lose his place if he agreed to remain beyond 2028.

His experience and leadership could allow PSG to manage the transition more gradually, although the club have not publicly outlined such a plan.

The discussions surrounding Marquinhos also form part of a wider effort to secure the futures of several influential members of Luis Enrique's squad.

According to Le Parisien, negotiations with Ousmane Dembele and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia are progressing well, with the former potentially extending his contract until 2030 and the Georgian winger until 2032.

PSG have reportedly maintained their intentions regarding Kvaratskhelia despite the serious knee injury he sustained against Barcelona in October.

Talks are also underway with Desire Doue, while the club are working to retain promising academy players Quentin Ndjantou and David Boly.

Marquinhos's situation remains less advanced than those of Dembele and Kvaratskhelia, and no agreement is imminent.

Nevertheless, the decision to explore another contract for their captain suggests that PSG are not yet ready to put a definitive timetable on his eventual succession.
